answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a ripple as the anchor of the cost.
